posts.caption: The knee pads are taking this more seriously than I am.
posts.translationZh: 護膝比我還認真看待這件事。
posts.storyContext: Max borrowed a skateboard for a short practice session at a quiet skatepark. Before trying anything, he sat down to adjust the knee pads that kept slipping when he bent his legs. The preparation looked less exciting than the skating clips he had watched, but it made him feel more settled. He can discuss beginning slowly, describe the first small movement he wants to learn, or compare trying something new alone with learning alongside a friend.
posts.imageAlt: Max seated at an empty skatepark bench, tightening a knee-pad strap beside a skateboard and helmet.

posts.caption: A neighbor shared one mint cutting. Now I’m the person checking leaves before breakfast.
posts.translationZh: 鄰居分給我一小段薄荷，現在我變成早餐前會先檢查葉子的人了。
posts.storyContext: Maya checked the mint cutting a neighbor had given her and noticed that its newest leaves looked firmer. She had worried after a warm afternoon left the little pot drooping. Moving it away from direct sun seemed to help. Watering it now feels like continuing a small conversation from the hallway. She can explain the plant’s progress, discuss the things neighbors share, or talk about a new routine that arrived through a simple gift.
posts.imageAlt: Maya crouching beside herb pots on an apartment balcony, watering the soil near a mint plant in soft daylight.

posts.caption: One cup left in the sink. A small ending to the day.
posts.translationZh: 水槽裡剩最後一個杯子。一天就這樣，有了個小小的結尾。
posts.storyContext: Noah had almost left a single cup in the sink until morning. Instead, he rinsed it while the kitchen was quiet and put it beside the others to dry. The task took less time than he had spent considering it. He liked seeing the counter clear before turning off the light. He can describe an evening routine, discuss the difference between a helpful habit and an obligation, or talk about the small signs that a day is finished.
posts.imageAlt: Noah rinsing a plain ceramic cup at his kitchen sink in warm evening light, wearing a dusty-rose shirt.

posts.caption: The fitted sheet and I have agreed to call this folded.
posts.translationZh: 我和這張床包已經達成共識：這樣就算摺好了。
posts.storyContext: Oscar started folding a clean fitted sheet with the quiet confidence of someone who had forgotten the previous attempt. The elastic corners immediately complicated his plan. After trying two different arrangements, he produced something that occupied less space without resembling a rectangle. He decided that was enough progress for one evening. He can describe his folding method, debate whether shape really matters in a cupboard, or share another chore with an unexpectedly flexible definition of finished.
posts.imageAlt: Oscar standing beside a sofa, gathering the elastic corners of a fitted sheet with a dry, bemused expression.

posts.caption: Brought the coffee with me. The bench supplied the rest.
posts.translationZh: 咖啡是我帶來的。剩下的，這張長椅都準備好了。
posts.storyContext: Ryan took a thermos to the park instead of buying another coffee on the way. The first bench was wet, so he walked a little farther and found a dry spot beneath a tree. Pouring slowly gave him a reason to stop checking his phone. Nothing especially remarkable happened, which suited him. He can describe the route, discuss a small habit that makes a break feel different, or talk about when saving money also improves the afternoon.
posts.imageAlt: Ryan seated on a park bench pouring coffee from a steel thermos into a cup, with trees and an open path behind.

posts.caption: That dial clicks into place like it means it.
posts.translationZh: 那顆旋鈕轉到定位時的聲音，聽起來很有主見。
posts.storyContext: Theo stopped at a secondhand electronics shop and noticed a portable radio with a beautifully solid tuning dial. He crouched beside the shelf and turned it carefully, enjoying the small mechanical clicks. The shop was quiet enough that the movement felt unusually noticeable. He can describe what drew him to the object, compare physical controls with touchscreens, or imagine a new device that would become more pleasant if one tiny interaction felt better.
posts.imageAlt: Theo crouching beside a shelf of secondhand electronics, turning the knob of a vintage portable radio with an attentive expression.

posts.caption: Stopped for a leaf I would usually have walked past.
posts.translationZh: 為一片平常會直接走過的葉子，停了一下。
posts.storyContext: Yuna noticed a yellow leaf beside the path and picked it up because a thin part of it caught the light. Holding it against the sun revealed a pattern she had not seen from the ground. She stayed still for a moment before continuing her walk. She can describe the color, discuss why the detail made her pause, or share another ordinary thing that became interesting after someone looked at it from a different angle.
posts.imageAlt: Yuna walking on an autumn park path while holding a yellow fallen leaf toward the light, wearing a muted blue coat.

posts.caption: I offered to walk the dog. He has kindly taken over the planning.
posts.translationZh: 我說要帶狗散步。牠很貼心，連行程都接手了。
posts.storyContext: Zoe offered to take a familiar dog for a short walk and quickly learned that short was not a shared measurement. Every patch of grass seemed to require a careful inspection. She stopped trying to choose the pace and followed the route at a comfortable distance. The detours were more entertaining than her original plan. She can describe the dog’s priorities, invent his review of the park, or discuss how an ordinary favor changed the shape of an afternoon.
posts.imageAlt: Zoe walking a friendly tan dog along a park path, holding a relaxed leash and watching the dog pause by the grass.

posts.caption: The cardboard box has been promoted to drawer management.
posts.translationZh: 紙箱升職了，現在負責管理抽屜。
posts.imageAlt: Ada crouching beside a low hallway cabinet, fitting plain cardboard dividers into an open drawer.
posts.storyContext: Ada kept a sturdy delivery box because the cardboard seemed too useful to throw away. It became dividers for the drawer where loose keys and cables kept disappearing. Her first strip was slightly too long, so she trimmed a narrow edge instead of forcing it. The compartments are simple and already useful. She can describe the fitting process, reveal what turned up in the drawer, or discuss a small everyday annoyance worth fixing.

posts.caption: One last ball. A phrase I’ve now used six times.
posts.translationZh: 最後一球。這句話我已經講了六次。
posts.imageAlt: Bella following a basketball toward an arcade hoop after releasing it, in a red sweatshirt and black joggers.
posts.storyContext: Bella discovered an arcade basketball machine and intended to play once before leaving. A few near misses made the next round feel irresistible. She changed her stance, slowed her throw, and finally watched one ball drop cleanly through the hoop. The celebration lasted longer than the shot. She can replay the sequence, argue for one more round, or talk about a harmless activity that becomes surprisingly difficult to walk away from.

posts.caption: Same story, different words. Now I’m reading both.
posts.translationZh: 同一個故事，不同的文字。現在兩本我都得讀了。
posts.imageAlt: Felix comparing two open books at a quiet library table, wearing a cream knitted sweater; no book text is readable.
posts.storyContext: Felix picked up two translations of the same story at the library. A sentence that sounded brisk in one felt hesitant in the other, and he began comparing how each version shaped the character. The plan to read a single chapter quietly became a much longer visit. He can describe the difference without needing to quote the text, talk about what translation changes, or invite another interpretation of a character whose intentions remain unclear.

posts.caption: Two skips. Enough to make me search for another stone.
posts.translationZh: 跳了兩下。已經足夠讓我繼續找下一顆石頭。
posts.storyContext: Finn found a quiet patch of pebbles beside the lake and started choosing stones flatter than his thumb. Several dropped straight into the water, while one managed two quick skips before disappearing. That tiny difference was enough to keep him there longer than planned. He stopped counting after a while and paid more attention to the ripples. He can explain how he chose a stone, compare attempts, or talk about an activity that becomes absorbing without needing much equipment.
posts.imageAlt: Finn finishing a low stone-skipping throw beside a pebbled lake, smiling across the water in a mustard windbreaker and olive trousers.

posts.caption: The soup was simple. The moving view did most of the seasoning.
posts.translationZh: 湯很簡單。窗外一路變換的景色，替它添了不少滋味。
posts.storyContext: Hugo ordered soup in the train dining car because he wanted something warm rather than another hurried snack. A bend in the track made him steady the bowl before his first spoonful. After that, he settled into the rhythm of the journey and watched fields pass the window. He can describe the meal, talk about eating while traveling, or compare a slow train lunch with food grabbed between connections.
posts.imageAlt: Hugo seated by a train dining-car window, pausing over tomato soup while watching the countryside.

posts.caption: The bird moved two centimetres. I celebrated like it had crossed an ocean.
posts.translationZh: 紙鳥只前進兩公分，我卻高興得像牠剛飛越一片海。
posts.storyContext: Iris tried making a tiny stop-motion scene with a paper bird and a phone. Moving the bird by small amounts was easy until her sleeve nudged the background. She reset the paper, slowed down, and watched the short sequence again. A few seconds of movement felt surprisingly rewarding. She can explain the simple setup, imagine where the bird goes next, or compare patient handmade effects with instant digital ones.
posts.imageAlt: Iris seated at a small table, moving a paper bird beneath an overhead phone for a stop-motion scene.

posts.caption: A room full of clocks, and I still forgot to check the time.
posts.translationZh: 滿屋子都是鐘，我卻還是忘了看時間。
posts.storyContext: Isla visited a small clock collection and became absorbed in the different sounds of the mechanisms. One slow pendulum seemed to set the pace for the room. She had planned a short visit but stayed longer than expected, listening between footsteps. She can describe the clock that caught her attention, imagine who once wound it each morning, or compare a useful object with the stories people attach to it.
posts.imageAlt: Isla leaning slightly toward a brass pendulum clock behind museum glass, hands loosely clasped at her waist.

posts.caption: This pebble has probably travelled further than I have. It is being very quiet about it.
posts.translationZh: 這顆石頭走過的路大概比我還多，只是它不太愛說。
posts.storyContext: Luna walked along the beach until a smooth gray pebble caught her attention. She turned it over in her hand and tried to imagine all the water that had shaped it. The stone offered no useful details, which left her plenty of room to make things up. Before leaving, she set it back among the others. She can invent its journey, describe the sound of the shore, or discuss why some small objects feel unusually old.
posts.imageAlt: Luna walking along a quiet pebble beach, holding a smooth stone and watching the waves.

posts.caption: Packed enough trail mix for a walk. Or a minor expedition.
posts.translationZh: 替散步準備了綜合堅果。這份量，大概也能應付一場小遠征。
posts.storyContext: Max decided to make a snack mix before going out for a walk. A handful of nuts became two, and the dried fruit made the container look smaller than expected. A few pieces escaped while he poured. He put the lid nearby and accepted that some would stay at home. He can explain what he chose, debate the best walking snack, or describe the small preparations that make a simple outing more enjoyable.
posts.imageAlt: Max pouring nuts and dried fruit into a reusable container in his kitchen, watching a few pieces spill onto the counter.

posts.caption: These keys once opened ordinary doors. I wish I knew whose.
posts.translationZh: 這些鑰匙曾經打開一扇扇普通的門。真想知道，那是誰家的門。
posts.storyContext: Maya paused at a museum case that held several old iron keys. The objects were simple, but their worn edges made her imagine the everyday doors they once opened. She found herself more curious about the people carrying them than about the locks. The short display could only answer part of that. She can describe the key that caught her eye, imagine an ordinary day around it, or discuss what makes a small object worth keeping.
posts.imageAlt: Maya studying antique iron keys in a glass museum case, hands loosely clasped, wearing a burgundy knitted top.

posts.caption: The book I noticed was on the shelf I nearly walked past.
posts.translationZh: 注意到的那本書，剛好在我差點直接走過的書架上。
posts.storyContext: Noah went to return a library book and crouched to check a low shelf on the way out. A slim volume reminded him of an author he had meant to try months earlier. He read a few lines while the rest of the aisle stayed quiet. There was no need to decide quickly. He can explain what caught his interest, discuss reading at his own pace, or talk about a small discovery made during a routine errand.
posts.imageAlt: Noah crouching beside a low library shelf, sliding out a slim book, wearing an oat cardigan over a navy shirt.

posts.caption: The comfortable pair has won. A deeply unglamorous victory.
posts.translationZh: 舒服的那雙贏了。一場非常不華麗的勝利。
posts.storyContext: Oscar tried on a pair of shoes that looked more impressive on the display than they felt on his feet. A plainer pair gave him considerably less to think about. He sat on the fitting bench and considered how rarely anyone compliments a comfortable walk. That seemed like a reasonable trade. He can compare the two pairs, discuss a purchase that improved daily life, or explain which sensible choice took him longest to make.
posts.imageAlt: Oscar seated on a shoe-shop bench, comparing a brown shoe on his foot with another held above his lap.

posts.caption: Dinner looks like I made more effort than I did.
posts.translationZh: 這頓晚餐看起來，比我實際花的功夫還多。
posts.storyContext: Ryan put pumpkin in the oven while finishing a few ordinary chores. He nearly forgot the tray, then caught the smell just as the edges began to brown. Dinner required less attention than he had expected and tasted better for the extra minute. He set the tray down before deciding what else to serve. He can describe the simple preparation, discuss meals worth repeating after work, or compare cooking something slowly with trying to get everything done at once.
posts.imageAlt: Ryan lifting a tray of roasted pumpkin at his home kitchen counter, wearing oven mitts and a charcoal apron.

posts.caption: I wanted better coffee. Apparently I also wanted measurements.
posts.translationZh: 我想喝好一點的咖啡。看來，我也想要一些測量數據。
posts.storyContext: Theo changed one thing about his morning coffee and immediately wanted to know what it had changed. He checked the water with a simple thermometer before pouring, then tried to remember how the previous cup had tasted. The comparison was less precise than the instrument suggested. He still enjoyed paying attention. He can describe the routine, discuss when measuring helps a hobby, or admit which parts of his supposedly careful experiment were mostly hopeful guesses.
posts.imageAlt: Theo checking a kettle with a small analog thermometer beside a coffee dripper at a home kitchen counter.

posts.caption: A little sprig of flowers. Quite a lot of patience.
posts.translationZh: 一小枝花，用掉不少耐心。
posts.storyContext: Yuna decided to embroider a small floral sprig on a plain handkerchief. The first stitches were too tight, so she loosened them and began again. She worked slowly enough to notice when her shoulders became tense. The little purple flowers are still modest and a little uneven. She can describe choosing the color, discuss learning a careful hand skill, or talk about an object that becomes more personal when someone spends time changing it.
posts.imageAlt: Yuna embroidering a small purple floral sprig in a hoop at a home sewing table under a warm lamp, wearing a lilac shirt.

posts.caption: Went in for basil. Apparently I now run a small forest.
posts.translationZh: 本來只想買點羅勒。看來我現在經營一座小森林。
posts.storyContext: Zoe visited the plant nursery for a modest pot of basil and found one that looked unusually enthusiastic about being alive. She sat it on her lap to work out how she would carry it home. The leaves smelled wonderful, which made the practical questions easier to postpone. Her kitchen window may need a rearrangement. She can discuss her ambitious purchase, imagine meals for the basil, or admit which small errand most recently expanded beyond its original brief.
posts.imageAlt: Zoe seated on a nursery stool with a lush potted basil plant on her lap, inspecting its leaves with an amused smile.

posts.caption: The wind is helping with the design review.
posts.translationZh: 風也來幫忙審查設計了。
posts.imageAlt: Ada kneeling on a beach mat, adjusting the strings of a small driftwood mobile in soft coastal light.
posts.storyContext: Ada collected a few small pieces of fallen driftwood from a permitted stretch of beach and tried tying them into a hanging mobile. The first arrangement leaned heavily to one side. Moving a knot worked better than adding another piece, and the breeze immediately tested the change. She likes the uneven shapes more than matching pieces. She can describe the balance problem or imagine what other ordinary materials might make an interesting mobile.

posts.caption: My suitcase found a reason to stay. I have a train to catch.
posts.translationZh: 行李箱找到留下來的理由了。但我還得趕火車。
posts.imageAlt: Bella bending beside a small suitcase on a station concourse, freeing a plain scarf from a wheel, wearing a lilac jacket.
posts.storyContext: Bella was crossing the station concourse when her suitcase began pulling stubbornly to one side. A loose scarf had caught around a wheel. She stepped out of the flow of travelers and worked the fabric free, relieved that nothing had torn. There was still enough time to reach the platform without running. She can recount the interruption, share her imperfect packing system, or discuss the little moments that turn a routine journey into a story.

posts.caption: No battery, no notifications. Quite a strong feature list.
posts.translationZh: 不用電池，也沒有通知。功能清單相當有競爭力。
posts.imageAlt: Felix pausing beside a stone sundial in a sunny botanical garden, looking at its shadow in a sage-green shirt.
posts.storyContext: Felix noticed a sundial while walking through a garden and stopped to compare its shadow with the time on his phone. The difference sent him looking for an explanation rather than assuming either object was wrong. He liked the way a familiar question became visible on stone. He can describe the shadow, explore why the readings might differ, or discuss an older tool that still makes an idea easier to understand than its modern replacement.

posts.caption: Breakfast is leaning slightly. I respect its commitment to staying upright.
posts.translationZh: 早餐有點歪。我很尊重它努力站穩的決心。
posts.storyContext: Finn decided a slow breakfast deserved pancakes and discovered that making them the same size required more patience than he had supplied. He stacked the small ones anyway, added a few blueberries, and watched the tower lean toward the edge of the plate. A careful nudge rescued it before syrup became involved. He can talk about the cooking attempt, describe his ideal unhurried breakfast, or defend why an uneven stack still counts as a successful start.
posts.imageAlt: Finn placing a pancake onto an uneven stack in his home kitchen, concentrating with a spatula in hand and a bowl of blueberries nearby.

posts.caption: The bag is nearly full. The coffee equipment remains non-negotiable.
posts.translationZh: 行李快滿了。咖啡器材這一項，沒有商量空間。
posts.storyContext: Hugo tried packing for a short trip with one small bag. Clothes fitted easily until he added his little coffee dripper. Moving a sweater created a space, but then the lid would not close comfortably. He took out a spare shirt and kept the dripper. The choice made him laugh. He can explain his packing priorities, compare travel essentials, or describe the smallest kitchen he has used away from home.
posts.imageAlt: Hugo kneeling beside an open suitcase at home, fitting a small coffee dripper among folded clothes.

posts.caption: Walk around one sculpture and it gives you three different arguments.
posts.translationZh: 繞著一座雕塑走一圈，它就能提出三種不同的說法。
posts.storyContext: Iris stopped at a curved sculpture that seemed heavy from one direction and almost weightless from another. She walked around it slowly, noticing how the gaps changed the background. A patch of sun appeared just as she reached the far side. She can describe the shape without naming it, compare her first impression with the second, or invent a short scene in which this object has an unexpected role.
posts.imageAlt: Iris walking beside a curved bronze sculpture in a garden, studying how its outline changes.

posts.caption: The narrator paused. I kept walking, but the sentence stayed with me.
posts.translationZh: 朗讀的人停了一下。我繼續走，那句話卻留了下來。
posts.storyContext: Isla listened to a story on her walk and noticed how the narrator used a pause to change an ordinary sentence. She slowed down rather than reaching immediately for the next part. The path was familiar, which left more room to listen. She can describe the mood without quoting the text, compare listening with reading a page, or discuss why a voice sometimes changes the way a character feels.
posts.imageAlt: Isla walking along a leafy park path with small earbuds, listening and looking toward the trees.

posts.caption: Built a very small door. Still deciding who gets the key.
posts.translationZh: 做了一扇很小的門。還在決定鑰匙要交給誰。
posts.storyContext: Luna saved a piece of delivery cardboard and turned it into a miniature doorway. The first door kept falling inward, so she widened the little base before trying again. Once it stood up, the empty space behind it seemed more interesting than the construction itself. She has not decided what the door should open onto. She can imagine its occupant, explain her simple fix, or invite someone to invent the room on the other side.
posts.imageAlt: Luna kneeling on a rug, assembling a tiny cardboard doorway with craft scraps nearby.

posts.caption: Ready for the canoe. First, a small argument with this buckle.
posts.translationZh: 準備划獨木舟。先跟這個扣環小小爭論一下。
posts.storyContext: Max arrived at the boathouse early enough to take his time getting ready. The life jacket fitted well, but its buckle needed one more adjustment before he felt comfortable. He checked it on the dock while the canoe waited beside him. The quiet water made the extra minute feel unimportant. He can describe the planned outing, talk about learning a new outdoor routine, or compare the excitement before an activity with the first few minutes of actually doing it.
posts.imageAlt: Max adjusting his orange life jacket on a dry wooden dock beside a moored canoe, looking down at the buckle.

posts.caption: Three strands of dough, and suddenly I’m thinking about everyone who taught someone to bake.
posts.translationZh: 三條麵團，卻讓我想到那些把烘焙手藝教給別人的人。
posts.storyContext: Maya tried braiding bread at a small bakery session. Keeping track of three soft strands took more attention than she expected, and one end became thicker than the other. The demonstration reminded her that a familiar food can hold many tiny learned movements. She decided to keep the uneven braid. She can describe the step that confused her, discuss learning by watching someone’s hands, or share a food that feels connected to a person rather than a place.
posts.imageAlt: Maya braiding three strips of bread dough at a bakery workbench, wearing a sage blouse and plain flour-dusted apron.

posts.caption: A leaf bigger than my notebook. I stayed with that thought for a while.
posts.translationZh: 一片比筆記本還大的葉子。這個念頭，讓我停留了一會兒。
posts.storyContext: Noah entered the glasshouse to get out of a brief shower and slowed down beside a broad leaf. Its pale veins seemed to divide the surface into smaller paths. He had expected to look at the brighter flowers, but this quiet detail held his attention longer. The rain softened against the roof above him. He can describe the leaf, compare busy and restful places, or talk about noticing something he had not planned to see.
posts.imageAlt: Noah pausing beside a large leaf on a botanical glasshouse path, hands in his jacket pockets and gaze on the leaf.

posts.caption: This leaf followed me for half the path. I admire the commitment.
posts.translationZh: 這片葉子跟了我半條步道。這份毅力，值得尊敬。
posts.storyContext: Oscar heard a faint scraping sound on the path and initially blamed the wind. The noise continued whenever he moved and stopped whenever he did, which narrowed the investigation considerably. A large leaf had caught beside his shoelace. He crouched to remove it and left it at the edge of the path. He can recount the unnecessarily slow discovery, describe the walk, or compare small annoyances that become funnier once their cause is obvious.
posts.imageAlt: Oscar crouching on an autumn park path, removing a large leaf caught beside his shoelace.

posts.caption: One loose strap was making the whole ride sound expensive.
posts.translationZh: 一條鬆掉的綁帶，讓整趟騎車聽起來都很傷荷包。
posts.storyContext: Ryan heard an unfamiliar rattle while cycling home and briefly imagined a repair bill. In the courtyard, he found that a loose bag strap had been tapping the frame. He crouched beside the bicycle and tightened it before checking the wheel once more. The silence afterward felt like a small bargain. He can explain how he found the noise, discuss everyday maintenance he actually enjoys, or share a moment when a worrying problem turned out to have a simple cause.
posts.imageAlt: Ryan crouching by a parked city bicycle to fasten a canvas pannier strap in a quiet residential courtyard.

posts.caption: Folded the wing a little differently. Now I have a research project.
posts.translationZh: 機翼多折了一點點。現在，我有個研究計畫了。
posts.storyContext: Theo folded a paper glider during a break and took it outside to see whether a small change would help it fly straighter. The first throw turned sharply, so he adjusted one wing and tried a gentler release. He kept comparing the flights instead of checking the time. He can describe the change, argue for a very informal testing method, or invent another small experiment using something simple enough to fit in a pocket.
posts.imageAlt: Theo walking on an open park lawn with a paper glider poised to launch, wearing an ochre overshirt and navy trousers.

posts.caption: A little of the beach insists on coming home.
posts.translationZh: 海灘有一小部分，堅持要跟我回家。
posts.storyContext: Yuna took a short walk along the beach and thought she had kept mostly to the firm sand. On the steps afterward, one shoe proved otherwise. She tipped it gently and waited for the last grains to fall before putting it back on. The small pause made leaving feel less abrupt. She can describe the walk, talk about a quiet place near water, or share an ordinary sign that a brief outing has followed someone home.
posts.imageAlt: Yuna seated on dry steps above a quiet beach, tipping sand from a shoe, with the shoreline behind her.

posts.caption: Found my balance. Please do not ask it any difficult questions.
posts.translationZh: 找到平衡感了。拜託先別問它太難的問題。
posts.storyContext: Zoe brought a yoga mat to the rooftop expecting a quiet stretch. A simple balancing pose turned out to require more negotiation than she had planned. She chose a fixed point across the roof, lowered her raised foot a little, and managed a few steady breaths. That was enough to count as an improvement. She can describe the adjustment, joke about her concentration, or compare small moments when slowing down was harder than doing more.
posts.imageAlt: Zoe balancing in a simple tree pose on a rooftop yoga mat, arms out and gaze fixed beyond the camera.

posts.caption: Halloween costume prop, day one: the bat wing holds. Day two: we find out if it flies.
posts.translationZh: 萬聖節服裝道具第一天：蝙蝠翅膀黏住了。第二天：看看它飛不飛得起來。
posts.imageAlt: Ada at a workshop table hot-gluing the ribs of a black cardboard bat-wing costume prop, wearing a mustard shirt and a green apron, smiling at her work.
posts.storyContext: Ada spent an afternoon at the community workshop turning leftover cardboard boxes and a torn black umbrella into a pair of bat wings for a neighbour's child to wear on Halloween. She scored the cardboard ribs, hot-glued the fabric in sections, and kept testing whether the wings would fold without cracking. The left wing still droops slightly, which she has decided adds character. She can explain how she reinforced the joints, suggest easy costume pieces made from things people already have, or talk about why handmade Halloween costumes are often the most memorable ones.

posts.caption: Witch hat or cat ears? I asked the shop mirror. The mirror said both, obviously.
posts.translationZh: 巫師帽還是貓耳朵？我問了店裡的鏡子。鏡子說：當然兩個都要。
posts.imageAlt: Bella laughing in a costume shop, holding up a black witch hat in one hand and a cat-ear headband in the other, wearing a denim shirt over a coral top.
posts.storyContext: Bella stopped into a small costume shop on the way home to find something simple for a friend's Halloween party, then spent twenty minutes trying to choose between a pointed witch hat and a cat-ear headband. Every time she held one up, the other looked funnier. She eventually admitted that the real costume plan was whatever made her laugh first in the mirror. She can talk about last-minute costume ideas, compare the easiest party looks to put together, or share the most ridiculous outfit she has ever seriously considered wearing.

posts.caption: Pumpkin patch rule: the weirdest gourd usually has the best story. This one has a lot to say.
posts.translationZh: 南瓜田守則：長得最奇怪的葫蘆，故事通常最精彩。這顆看起來有很多話要說。
posts.imageAlt: Felix crouching in a sunny pumpkin patch among orange pumpkins and hay bales, holding and studying a bumpy green gourd, wearing a navy sweater and khakis.
posts.storyContext: Felix visited a pumpkin patch outside the city intending to pick one classic round pumpkin for the windowsill, and instead found himself crouched among the rows studying a knobbly green gourd that looked nothing like the others. He turned it over several times, noticing how its strange shape seemed more interesting the longer he looked. He brought both home in the end. He can talk about why imperfect things often catch our attention, describe the different pumpkins and gourds he saw, or ask which seasonal tradition feels most like autumn to you.

posts.caption: Finished the Halloween fun run in a cape. Turns out capes are great for drama, terrible for headwind.
posts.translationZh: 穿著斗篷跑完萬聖節趣味路跑。原來斗篷很有戲劇效果，但逆風時超級吃虧。
posts.imageAlt: Finn stretching on a park path after a Halloween fun run, wearing a black cape over a grey tee with a plain orange race bib, orange pennant bunting overhead.
posts.storyContext: Finn joined a relaxed neighbourhood Halloween fun run in the park, where most runners wore something festive. He chose a simple black cape over his usual running shirt, which looked great at the start line and then caught every gust along the river path. After crossing the finish under strings of orange bunting, he stretched out his legs and laughed about how much harder the cape made the last kilometre. He can share tips for enjoying a casual themed run, talk about keeping exercise playful, or suggest costume pieces that are actually easy to move in.

posts.caption: Evening Halloween market: one caramel apple, a hundred glowing pumpkins, zero regrets.
posts.translationZh: 萬聖節夜市：一顆焦糖蘋果、一百顆發光的南瓜燈，毫無遺憾。
posts.imageAlt: Hugo smiling at an evening Halloween market holding a caramel apple on a stick, wearing a rust corduroy overshirt and navy scarf, glowing jack-o'-lanterns beside him.
posts.storyContext: Hugo wandered through a seasonal evening market while visiting a new town, following the smell of cinnamon and roasted nuts past stalls lined with carved, glowing pumpkins. He bought a caramel apple mainly because it looked like the most honest local dessert available, then discovered it was much stickier than expected. He kept walking slowly to take in the lights and the music. He can describe the stalls and seasonal snacks he found, compare autumn markets he has visited while travelling, or suggest a favourite treat to try at a festival.

posts.caption: Painted a few friendly ghosts on the café window. They're shy, so they only come out in October.
posts.translationZh: 在咖啡店窗上畫了幾隻友善的小幽靈。它們很害羞，只在十月出來見人。
posts.imageAlt: Iris painting smiling white ghosts and small orange pumpkins on a café window, holding a brush and a paint palette, wearing denim overalls over a mustard top.
posts.storyContext: A neighbourhood café asked Iris to decorate its front window for Halloween, with one request: nothing that would frighten small children. She sketched a row of round, smiling ghosts and little pumpkins, then painted them directly on the glass with washable window paint so they could be wiped away in November. The ghost on the far left came out slightly lopsided, and she liked it best. She can explain how window painting differs from canvas, share ideas for gentle seasonal decorations, or talk about drawing cute characters that still feel full of personality.

posts.caption: October reading list: ghost stories, a warm lantern, and a pumpkin keeping me company.
posts.translationZh: 十月書單：鬼故事、一盞溫暖的提燈，還有一顆南瓜陪著我。
posts.imageAlt: Isla curled in a leather armchair in a cozy library corner at dusk, reading an old book, a lit lantern and a small carved pumpkin on the shelf behind her, wearing a green cardigan.
posts.storyContext: Isla found a quiet armchair in the corner of the library as the light faded and settled in with a collection of old-fashioned ghost stories, the kind that are more atmospheric than frightening. The librarian had set out a small lantern and a carved pumpkin for the season, which made the corner feel like the setting of one of the tales. She read until the closing announcement. She can recommend gentle spooky stories for autumn evenings, talk about why old ghost tales still charm readers, or imagine the quiet history of the library corner itself.

posts.caption: Carved a moon and a star into my pumpkin, so now it can light up the night all by itself.
posts.translationZh: 在南瓜上刻了月亮和星星，現在它可以自己點亮整個夜晚了。
posts.imageAlt: Luna in a night park holding a glowing jack-o'-lantern carved with a crescent moon and a star, looking up at it, wearing a cream sweater, autumn leaves around her.
posts.storyContext: Luna decided her jack-o'-lantern this year should look less like a face and more like a tiny piece of the night sky, so she carved a crescent moon and a single star above its smile. She carried it to the park after dark, where falling leaves drifted through the warm light from the string lamps. Holding it up, she imagined the pumpkin was a small moon that had wandered down to visit. She can share her carving design ideas, talk about stories inspired by the night sky, or invent a whimsical backstory for a pumpkin that wants to be a moon.

posts.caption: Entered the corn maze with a plan. Leaving with a pumpkin and absolutely no sense of direction.
posts.translationZh: 帶著計畫走進玉米迷宮，最後抱著一顆南瓜出來，方向感完全歸零。
posts.imageAlt: Max walking along a dirt path in a golden corn maze under a blue sky, a pumpkin tucked under one arm, grinning sheepishly, wearing a red plaid flannel and olive trousers.
posts.storyContext: Max went to a farm's autumn corn maze confident that his hiking experience would get him through in record time. Forty minutes later, he had passed the same bent stalk at least three times, picked up a pumpkin from a farm stand halfway through, and accepted that he was simply enjoying the walk now. The bright afternoon and rustling corn made getting lost feel like part of the fun. He can describe his very unreliable navigation strategy, compare the maze with real trails, or suggest other autumn outdoor activities worth trying.

posts.caption: Front steps are officially in Halloween mode. Every pumpkin got a say in where it sits.
posts.translationZh: 門前台階正式進入萬聖節模式。每顆南瓜要坐哪裡，都有經過它們同意。
posts.imageAlt: Maya crouching on brick front steps arranging pumpkins, autumn leaves and a glowing paper lantern, smiling toward the street, wearing a burnt-orange blouse and gold hoops.
posts.storyContext: Maya spent a golden afternoon decorating the front steps of her townhouse for Halloween, arranging pumpkins of different sizes, a paper lantern, autumn leaves and a dried corn-husk bundle by the door. She moved each pumpkin several times until the steps felt balanced but welcoming, imagining how they would look to children arriving for treats. A neighbour waved as she placed the last one. She can share how she styles simple seasonal displays, talk about decorations that welcome a neighbourhood, or describe the small joy of preparing a home for a holiday.
